consent.description: A consent assertion exchanged between two Pryv accounts as part of a cross-account access lifecycle (request → accept | refuse → revoke). Each format represents one state-transition in the consent state machine, plus the post-acceptance handshake step and scope-change continuations. The class is shared by the CMC plugin (open-pryv.io `components/cmc`) and may be reused by other consent-style protocols.

request-cmc.description: Cross-account consent request issued by a requester (`cmc/request-v1` lineage). The plugin mints a single-use capability access from this trigger, embeds the URL in `content.capabilityUrl`, and delivers the request to the recipient.

to.description: Recipient identity, or `null` for an open invite to be claimed via the capability URL.

capabilityRequested.description: When true, the plugin mints a single-use capability URL the recipient can open out-of-band.

request.description: The consent assertion: localised title/description/consent text + the requested permissions + optional features and expiry.

title.description: Localized text: language-code (2-3 lowercase letters) → string.

mandatory.description: Consent-layer flag: this entry is required for the requesting app to function - an accept must include it (the consent UI locks it; the user's alternative is denying the whole request).

optIn.description: Consent-layer flag: this entry is optional and the consent UI opens it NOT pre-selected (the user opts in). Omit it for the default, where an optional entry opens pre-selected and the user may opt out. Display-only: it never changes what may be granted, and it cannot be combined with `mandatory` on the same entry.

optIn.description: Consent-layer flag: this entry is optional and the consent UI opens it NOT pre-selected (the user opts in). Omit it for the default, where an optional entry opens pre-selected and the user may opt out. Display-only: it never changes what may be granted, and it cannot be combined with `mandatory` on the same entry.

expiresAt.description: Absolute expiry of the capability access, Unix timestamp (seconds). Omit for the platform default (7 days). `null` requests a capability without expiry; the core accepts it for `capability.mode: 'open-link'` only and refuses it on single-use invites.

allowUserChoice.description: Default false: the consent is ALL OR NOTHING (the user may only accept the whole permission set or deny). Set true to let the user cherry-pick entries on the consent screen (entries flagged `mandatory` stay locked).

accessType.description: Pryv access type the accepted data-grant is minted as. Default `shared` (a non-delegable grant that cannot call `accesses.*`). Set `app` to make the grant delegable: the approved requester can `accesses.create` scoped, individually-named sub-accesses (permissions ⊆ the grant) for least-privilege re-delegation with per-actor audit attribution.

membership.description: Default false. Set true when the requester asks to join the accepter's group: the access the accepter mints is a membership access (role `member`) through which the member writes `consent/member-access-cmc` on the group's scope streams. Enforced by the platform, on write and again at accept: stream permissions only, on user-creatable `:_cmc:apps:<app>[:<path>]` streams, level `read` or `contribute`; no feature permissions; `accessType` absent or `shared`; `allowUserChoice` is treated as true whatever is sent (the accepter picks the scopes). A violation is refused with `cmc-membership-permissions-invalid`.

accept-cmc.description: Cross-account consent accept (`cmc/accept-v1` lineage). Has two shapes: LOCAL TRIGGER (carries `capabilityUrl`, written by the accepter's app to start the accept flow) OR PEER-DELIVERED (carries `grantedAccess.apiEndpoint` + server-stamped `from`, written by the accepter's plugin to the requester's responses stream / inbox).

capabilityUrl.description: Local-trigger shape: capability URL from the request.

accessName.description: Optional name for the data-grant access the accepter mints.

grantedPermissions.description: Optional consent downgrade: grant only this subset of the request's permissions (exact-entry identity; validated against the offer by the accepter's plugin).

extra.description: Deprecated: ignored by the platform. Use `features`.

features.description: The relationship's channels. On the local trigger: the features the accepter asks for, which can only narrow the offer's (`content.request.features`; each one is on unless set to `false`). The platform resolves the relationship's value from the offer and records it on the completed trigger and on the peer-delivered accept.

grantedAccess.description: Peer-delivered shape: data-grant URL the accepter minted on their account.

from.description: Server-stamped at inbox-write time from the back-channel access's stored counterparty identity.

refuse-cmc.description: Cross-account consent refuse (`cmc/refuse-v1` lineage). Carries the capability URL of the request being refused + an optional localised reason.

revoke-cmc.description: Cross-account consent revoke (`cmc/revoke-v1` lineage). Either party tears down an established access pair by writing this with the local data-grant access id + an optional localised reason.

back-channel-cmc.description: Post-acceptance handshake step (`cmc/back-channel-v1` lineage). Delivered from the requester to the accepter's `:_cmc:inbox` via the data-grant URL, carrying the requester's back-channel apiEndpoint + remote stream-ids so the accepter can later POST chat / system messages back to the requester.

scope-request-cmc.description: Collector-proposed scope change on an established consent (`cmc/system-scope-request-v1` lineage). The collector writes a proposal carrying the desired new permissions; the user-side app accepts or refuses by writing a corresponding `consent/scope-update-cmc` event.

scope-update-cmc.description: User-side scope change apply / notify (`cmc/system-scope-update-v1` lineage). Has two shapes: response-to-request (carries `scopeRequestEventId` + `accept`) OR self-initiated (carries `newPermissions`). The plugin updates the local data-grant access permissions and notifies the peer.

invalidate-link-cmc.description: Requester-side invalidation of an open-link consent capability (`cmc/invalidate-link-v1` lineage). The plugin flips the capability access state to `'invalidated'` so further accepts are rejected. Already-established data-grant + back-channel relationships are UNTOUCHED — use `consent/revoke-cmc` for per-relationship teardown. Single-use capabilities are auto-consumed on first accept; calling invalidate on a single-use capability is a no-op.

member-access-cmc.description: A group member asks the group's core for a short-lived access on a patient's account. Written on the group account, on a scope stream the member's membership access holds `contribute` on (or by the group's personal token). The group's core mints a `shared` child access on the patient's core through the data-grant it holds, named and attributed by the server, and returns its apiEndpoint once, in the `memberAccess` field of the synchronous `events.create` response (never stored on the event). Server-owned fields (`status`, `failure`, `memberAccess`, `member`, `relationshipAccessId`) are written by the platform after dispatch and never by a client: a client-supplied value is discarded on create, and the stored value is kept on update.

counterparty.description: The patient: the counterparty of the group's relationship whose data-grant is used.

host.description: The counterparty's canonical host, as stored on the group's relationship access (`clientData.cmc.counterparty.host`), not the hostname of a per-user API URL.

scopeStreamId.description: Scope stream of the patient relationship. Default: the trigger's stream; must equal it or be under it.

permissions.description: Stream permissions of the child access, a subset of the offer's stream permissions outside `:_cmc:` (level not above the offer's). Default: the offer's stream permissions outside `:_cmc:`, at level `read`. Feature permissions are refused; the patient's core enforces the data-grant as the final bound.

expireAfter.description: Lifetime of the child access, in seconds. Default and bounds are per core (`cmc:memberAccess:defaultTtl`, `minTtl`, `maxTtl`; 24 hours, 60 seconds and 7 days by default), and never beyond the data-grant's own expiry.

status.description: Server-owned: dispatch state of the trigger.

failure.description: Server-owned, present when `status` is `failed`: `reason` is an error id (e.g. `cmc-member-access-grant-not-delegable`, `cmc-member-access-peer-rejected`, `cmc-member-access-peer-unreachable`, `cmc-member-access-membership-gone`, `cmc-member-access-not-retryable`); `detail` carries at most `peerErrorId` and `httpStatus`, never a peer response body.

memberAccess.description: Server-owned, on success: the child access minted on the patient's core. Never carries its token or apiEndpoint.

attribution.description: `stamped`: the child access carries the member and group identity in its `clientData.cmc`, set by the patient's core. `name-only`: the patient's core runs an older release that refuses the stamp; only the access name identifies the member.

member.description: Server-owned: the member, taken from the membership access that wrote the trigger.

relationshipAccessId.description: Server-owned: id of the group's access for the patient relationship used.

member-revoke-cmc.description: Offboarding of a group member: removes the child accesses minted for that member on patients' cores. Written by the platform on the group's scope stream whenever a membership ends (revoked, deleted, expired, narrowed, delegation detached, account deleted); a client write is refused with `cmc-protected-event-write`, and every field is server-owned (a client-supplied value is discarded on create, and the stored value is kept on update). Records who was offboarded and what was removed, with the outcome per child access.

status.description: Server-owned: dispatch state of the trigger.

failure.description: Server-owned, present when `status` is `failed`: `reason` is an error id (e.g. `cmc-member-revoke-residual`); `detail` carries at most `childAccessId`, `peerErrorId` and `httpStatus`, never a peer response body.

outcome.description: Server-owned: the result per child access, read back on the patient's core.

result.description: `deleted`: removed now. `absent`: already gone or expired. `residual`: still present (patient's core unreachable or refusing); retried, and bounded by the child's own expiry.

residuals.description: Server-owned: the child accesses that could not be removed.

expires.description: Unix timestamp (seconds): the latest the residual can live.
